name: Roman terra sigillata
region: Arezzo, Italy; later southern and central Gaul
summary: Red-gloss tableware of the Roman world. Potters at Arezzo press fine clay into stamped moulds, coat the pieces with a slip of very small particles, and fire them to a glossy coral red.

philosophy.core_thesis: A fine slip, not a glaze, gives the red shine: the potter sorts the clay by particle size, paints the thin top layer on the pot, and fires it in clean air.
design_principles: Settle the clay in water and keep only the finest top layer, with particles under 1 micron, for the slip.
Coat the leather-hard pot with 1 or 2 thin layers of slip and polish it with a soft cloth.
Press the bowl into a fired clay mould that carries the relief in reverse; the mould keeps the design sharp.
Stamp the maker name in a small cartouche in the well of the plate.
Give each form a fixed number in a catalogue, so that a buyer in any province can match the set.
Fire the ware in clean oxidising air at about 1000 °C, so that the iron in the slip turns red.
Stack the pieces in a large kiln in columns, with a ring of clay between them, to fire 10 000 or more at once.
anti_patterns: A glass-like glaze that fuses with the body and hides the clay
Black or grey patches from smoke in the kiln
Painted scenes with an outline brush on the red ground
A thick, wide-rimmed form with a heavy wall

form.shape: Plain and moulded plates, platters, bowls with relief friezes, and small cups with a lipped rim.
form.profile: A plate has a flat floor and a low wall that rises at an angle; a moulded bowl has a rounded body with a frieze of figures and a plain rim band.
form.foot_and_rim: A low ring foot, turned sharp on the wheel; the rim is a plain band or a thin rolled lip, often with a groove.
form.proportion: Plate diameter 15 to 30 cm and wall 3 to 5 mm thick, which is thin for earthenware.
rules: Keep the wall thin and even, so that the ware stacks and fires with little loss.
Divide a moulded bowl into one wide frieze and one narrow rim band.
Repeat the same form in 3 or 4 sizes, so that the set nests.

bodies.rule: Use a fine, iron-rich clay that fires to a dense red body at 1000 °C. Do not use porcelain or stoneware: the style is low-fired and unglazed.

methods: throwing plain plates on the wheel
press moulding bowls in a fired clay mould
stamping the maker name with a small die
forming.joins: Handles and applied figures are luted with slip; a bowl comes out of its mould when the clay has dried a little.
forming.details: A sharp foot ring, a circular maker stamp, and a slight seam where the frieze meets the rim band.

glaze.pattern: Friezes of dancers, plants, hunters and mythic scenes in low relief, with stamped palmettes and rosettes; plain plates carry only a maker stamp.
glaze.gloss: Soft sheen to gloss, about 25 to 45 GU; the shine comes from the polished slip.
glaze.wear: The slip scratches and wears at the foot and rim, and the buff or orange body shows under the red.

palette.strategy: One coral-red slip on an orange body, with a darker red in the deep relief.

firing.kiln: A large updraught kiln with a stack of ware in columns, fired with wood or charcoal.
processes: single firing in clean oxidising air
firing.scale: A workshop at Arezzo made thousands of pieces in one firing; the potteries of Gaul sent samian ware to the whole empire.
firing.signs: A maker stamp in the well, a small ring of kiln-stack marks on the foot, and an even red from rim to base.

pieces.form: Moulded bowl with a frieze of dancers and a plain rim band
Plain plate with a flat floor, an angled wall and a stamp in the well
Small plate with an incised rouletted line under the rim
Wide platter with a low wall and a groove at the rim

positive: stamped maker cartouche in the well

canonical_works.work: Moulded bowl stamped by Marcus Perennius Tigranus
canonical_works.maker: Workshop of Marcus Perennius Tigranus, Arezzo

canonical_works.work: Samian ware bowl of form Dragendorff 37

evidence.title: Samian ware bowl fragment, 1st century AD

emotion.target_response: A calm, civic confidence: the viewer sees a clean red set from a Roman table, made in great number and in one standard.

use_cases: a museum label on Roman tableware
a set or scene prompt for a Roman dining room
avoid_when: the brief needs a glossy glass glaze
the brief wants a painted scene on a black ground
the brief is for a modern food-safe glaze

modifiers.how: Change the red slip to a black gloss with painted figures that keep the red of the clay.
Change the body to a white porcelain with a clear glaze and drop the red slip and the stamped relief.
Change the body to porcelain, paint cobalt under a clear glaze, and keep the set of nesting plates.

wall_thickness.note: Thin walls are the sign of good sigillata.
